Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Australia's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Kate Pelle and Ines McKeon will open the innings. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Nishita Akter Nishi. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Australia will be the happier of the two sides, but the chase is not going to be straightforward. They will face a steady dose of spin on a wicket that has offered plenty of turn. If Bangladesh can strike early, the belief in their camp will only grow stronger. This has all the makings of a low-scoring thriller. Buckle up!

Tegan Williamson is in for a chat. She says it felt good to have a full spell and she tried to target the stumps to be in the game. Adds that she looks to keep things simple and looks up to Alana King and idolises her. Mentions that they have prepared well and are in a great mindset and the chase shouldn't be a tough one.

Five missed chances in the field and 13 wides are uncharacteristic numbers for any Australian side but Bangladesh simply failed to capitalize. Afia Ashima Era looked impressive and brought some much-needed momentum to the innings with her arrival. However, in the final five overs, she scarcely got the strike, halting any chance of a late flourish. Leggie Tegan Williamson stood out with the ball for Australia with figures of 2 for 12 in 4 overs.

Australia finish on a high and will be pleased with their effort. Conceding only 17 runs in the last 5 overs, they ensured that Bangladesh fell short of the three-figure mark. It was a tale of Australia steadily chipping away at the wickets at regular intervals, despite not being at their best with the ball or in the field. For Bangladesh, their innings was plagued by a staggering 73 dot balls and the lack of meaningful partnerships meant they never found any rhythm.

Afia is nowhere in the frame and Australia Women Under-19 manage to keep Bangladesh to just 91 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities behind us, it's now time for the action to get underway! The umpires make their way out to the middle and both teams are seen in a huddle having some final pep talk before stepping onto the field. Australia Women Under-19 burst open and take the field. Mst Sumaiya Akther Suborna and Fahomida Choya are the openers for Bangladesh Women Under-19. Chloe Ainsworth has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings. Here we go!
The match officials and the players make their way out for the national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's anthem first followed by that of Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Julia Price is down in the middle. She tells that it is a really hot day but importantly, there is no rain forecast. Tells that the outfield is a little bit wet and the batters should look to hit over the top, something that Australia did in the last game. Mentions that there will be help for both pacers and spinners. Further says that due to the deck's tacky nature, she feels the balls could hold up in the wicket for spinners.
Sumaiya Akter, the skipper of Bangladesh Women Under-19 says they would have bowled first as well considering the heavy outfield.

The captain of Australia, Lucy Hamilton says that the outfield is a little bit wet and feels that the wicket could have something in it early on. Tells that they are aware of what Bangladesh can do but for them, it is about playing to their strength.

Bangladesh Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Fahomida Choya, Juairiya Ferdous (WK), Mst Sumaiya Akther Suborna, Sumaiya Akter (C), Afia Ashima Era, Jannatul Maoua, Sadia Akter, Sadia Islam, Habiba Islam Pinky, Nishita Akter Nishi, Mst Anisa Akter Soba.

Australia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Kate Pelle, Ines McKeon, Lucy Hamilton (C), Caoimhe Bray, Eleanor Larosa, Hasrat Gill, Chloe Ainsworth, Grace Lyons (WK), Tegan Williamson, Juliette Morton, Amy Hunter.
TOSS - Australia Women Under-19 win the toss and have opted to BOWL first.

As for Bangladesh, they faced Nepal in their opener and, thanks to their spinners, bowled the opposition out for just 52. However, they did lose 5 wickets in the process, which they would have hoped to avoid for a more clinical performance. The Bangladeshi batters will face a tough challenge against Australia's pace attack, and the task will be even more difficult with the expected overcast conditions. These two sides met during the 2023 edition in Benoni, where Bangladesh came out on top. Can Australia reverse the result this time and secure their place in the Super Six? Stick around for the toss and team news.

Starting with Australia, they began their campaign in clinical fashion, with their pacers combining to bowl Scotland out for 48. The Australian batters then chased down the target in just 6.4 overs, giving their net run rate an early boost. Australia now face arguably the strongest test of the group stage, and it will be intriguing to see how they handle the Bangladeshi spinners as they look to make it two wins from two.

Hello and welcome to a Group D clash between Australia Women Under-19 and Bangladesh Women Under-19 at the YSD-UKM Cricket Oval in Bangi. Both teams started their campaigns with a win, and the winner of this clash will seal their place in the Super Six. The top three teams from each group will advance to the next round.
... MATCH DAY ...

With the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup in full swing, attention now shifts to Match 9, where Australia Women Under-19 face off against Bangladesh Women Under-19 in Group D. Both teams began their campaigns emphatically, registering crushing victories in their respective opening clashes. Australia, led by Lucy Hamilton, delivered a clinical performance against Scotland, showcasing their depth and dominance. The bowling attack, spearheaded by Eleanor Larosa and Caoimhe Bray, ran through the opposition, setting the tone for a strong campaign. The batters backed it up with a solid display, and with a squad rich in talent and balance, Australia looks like a formidable force heading into this clash. Bangladesh Women Under-19, on the other hand, dismantled Nepal in their opener with an astounding victory. Captain Sumaiya Akter, with her experience, has been the backbone of the side, and her leadership will be crucial as they aim to go further than their 2023 performance. Jannatul Maoua shone with the ball in the opening game, while Habiba Islam Pinky and Nishita Akter Nishi are emerging as key players to watch. However, the team’s batting, which appeared slightly shaky, will need to step up against a dominant Australian side. While the scales seem to tilt in Australia’s favour given their strength and momentum, Bangladesh have the talent and determination to put up a strong fight and possibly spring a surprise. Expect an exciting contest!
